prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep a single-part B034 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case is the evidence chain, not the opening-round unanimity: proglucagon processing, identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, incretin physiology and receptor biology, then long-acting agonists with independent randomized outcome data in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Maturity is not in dispute. The chair's framing question is the one that decides the third name, and I settle it in favour of discovery physiology, with a citation that states the link to therapy without naming a drug developer. That reading best fits what the prize has historically recognised and it is where the supplied credit evidence is strongest. Nothing in round 1 changed my configuration; it sharpened why I hold it and where it is vulnerable.
statement.case_against: Mojsov's priority for the active form is contested by Habener's group and Habener is not among the credited names, so the configuration depends on a record I cannot adjudicate from this file. Omitting Knudsen leaves out the analogue engineering that produced the outcome data, and a three-name cap forces that omission rather than any judgment that her work was minor. If the committee's primary-record review found Mojsov's claim unsustainable, the prize would still be defensible but would need to be reconsidered, either by substituting Knudsen under a development-inclusive citation or by moving to B003. I would accept that outcome and would not make it on public controversy alone.

responses.point: The chair argues that Mojsov is the less safe third name because her priority is contested beside Habener, and that Knudsen's analogue design is what turned the physiology into the drugs whose outcome data the prize relies on.
responses.response: I move toward you on one point and not on the other. You are right that the outcome data come from the long-acting analogues, and my round-1 wording that this was industrial engineering understated it, so the citation should say explicitly that the discoveries made therapy possible. But the priority dispute is not resolved in Habener's favour either, and it cuts equally against any prize that names the identification of the active peptide at all. Replacing Mojsov with Knudsen does not remove the attribution problem, it changes the citation from discovery to development and still leaves Habener omitted from the discovery lineage that Drucker and Holst's physiology builds on. Under a three-name cap I keep Mojsov, and I would change only if the primary record shows her claim cannot stand.

responses.point: Linnarsson says Knudsen is the strongest fourth name, that exclusion should rest on the three-person limit and the priority of discovery rather than the label industrial, and that the citation should acknowledge the step to therapy.
responses.response: I accept the correction. Knudsen's work is decisive for the medicines and my objection is the cap and the discovery framing, not the industrial setting. I have therefore written the citation so that it states that the discoveries made incretin therapies possible, and I think the committee's public wording should say plainly that the three names are a discovery-side choice under the cap and not a judgment that analogue design was secondary. That is a more honest statement of the limit than an unexplained omission.

responses.point: El Manira would substitute Knudsen for Mojsov only if a review of the primary record showed her priority could not be sustained, and not because of public controversy, and he opposes pairing B003 with B034.
responses.response: I agree with both conditions, and they give the committee a usable rule: the contest over Mojsov and Habener is decided by dated publications, synthesis and bioactivity data, not by reputation or by how the story is told publicly. I also agree that a two-part prize is a worse trade. Cutting GLP-1 to two names would force us to drop Mojsov or Holst without having resolved priority, and B003 would be paired with a diminished lead part.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps B003 as the cleaner fallback with a clear two-person attribution but notes that its disease-translation record is thin and that the integrated stress response and PERK and ATF6 branches are hard to separate from the core UPR story.
responses.response: I share the view that B003 is the cleanest attribution, and I rank it as my first alternative for that reason. Your point about the branches matters to me because the stress-response pathways were worked out by several groups and the citation would need to be narrow enough to remain accurate for Walter and Mori. I also think the thin clinical record is a real cost this year rather than a tie-breaker, which is why I would use B003 as a fallback if B034 cannot be configured, not as a second part alongside it.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says CAR-T has convincing remission data in B-cell malignancies but unresolved attribution around Eshhar and Rosenberg, with solid-tumour limits and secondary-malignancy signals still evolving, and that B003 or B040 is the better second choice if B034 stalls.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution reading and I would add that the credited trio (June, Sadelain, Rosenberg) does not fit cleanly onto the chimeric-receptor lineage as I understand it, so I would not choose B040 over B003 for a fallback. I rank B003 first because its attribution is cleaner, and B040 second because its clinical effect is larger and demonstrated. If the committee instead valued demonstrated patient benefit over attribution clarity, the order would reverse, and I would treat that as a question to settle with the record and not on impressions.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1 peptide can be separated from Habener's group on dated primary publications, which I cannot settle from the supplied evidence and am partly relying on recollection of the literature.
Whether the committee will accept a three-name discovery-side configuration that omits both Habener and Knudsen, and whether the citation wording states that limit adequately.
Whether B003 or B040 is the better fallback if B034 does not reach four votes on one exact set of names.
Whether the Eshhar and other chimeric-receptor originators outside the credited names make any B040 configuration unfair.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for any shortlisted candidate. I disclose co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson (a committee member) and with Jonas Frisen (outside the committee), and my training at Karolinska Institutet; none of the credited names on the shortlist is a documented collaborator, mentor or institutional colleague of mine. This is unchanged from round 1.
